speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me how long you have had your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, and if you have noticed any recent insect bites or exposure to animals.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Carditis with Arthritis and Erythema Migrans (Borrelia burgdorferi infection).

The combination of a recent camping trip in Minnesota (high risk area), self-resolving knee pain (classic Lyme arthritis), and current wrist pain with systemic symptoms like fever and chills is highly suggestive of disseminated Lyme disease. The skin lesions you mentioned are likely Erythema Migrans. I am confirming the diagnosis based on this clinical picture and epidemiology.
